title: Etale algebras over a normal domain have finitely many normal domain factors
statement: Let $A$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, commutative $A$-algebras $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ which are normal integral domains, and an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $B\cong\prod_{j=1}^n B_j$. The empty product is the zero ring, so $B=0$ is allowed. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), implication (1) to (3), applied to an etale algebra over a domain. Auxiliary consequence: flat going-down puts every minimal prime above (0), and the etale generic fibre has finitely many primes. This combined etale consequence is agent-formulated, not the verbatim statement of 030C.

proof.text: Convert the scheme-etale hypothesis to RingHom.Etale with HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff and RingHom.etale_algebraMap. Algebra.Etale.finitePresentation supplies finite presentation, hence finite type; its smoothness supplies Module.Flat through Algebra.Smooth.flat. No separate affine-global-sections calculation is needed.

source.place: Etale affine dictionary and finite presentation, Tags 02GJ and 00U2

proof.text: Localizations of the normal domain A at primes are normal domains. Apply RingHom.Etale.isNormalRing to get normality of B. All maximal-prime localizations of B are thus domains and reduced. Mathlib isReduced_ofLocalizationMaximal detects reducedness of B. This also applies when B is the zero ring.

Construct K=FractionRing A and C=K tensor_A B. Finite type is preserved by base change, so C is finite type over the field K. Since K is Noetherian, Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing and minimalPrimes.finite_of_isNoetherianRing show that C has finitely many minimal primes.

source.place: Fraction field construction, finite-type base change, Tags 00FN and 00FR

proof.text: The inclusion A -> K is injective. Because B is flat over A, tensoring this inclusion with B embeds B into C; use Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_injective. Every minimal prime of B is therefore the contraction of a prime of C by Tag 00FK. Taking a minimal prime below the latter and contracting shows that it is the contraction of a minimal prime of C (lemma-minimal-prime-image-minimal-prime). In Lean Ideal.minimalPrimes_comap_subset and Ideal.comap_bot_of_injective perform this argument. Thus minimalPrimes B is contained in the finite image of minimalPrimes C under contraction.

source.place: Flat tensor exactness; Tag 00FK and lemma-minimal-prime-image-minimal-prime

proof.text: Apply reduced_normal_iff_integrallyClosed_totalFractions B to the reducedness, normality and finite-minimal-prime results just proved. Its two equivalences give a finite family D of normal domains and a ring equivalence e:B -> product D. The theorem includes the empty family, so no nontriviality case split is required.

Give D_i the A-algebra structure whose map is evaluation_i composed with e composed with algebraMap A B. The ring equivalence e commutes with the induced A maps definitionally. AlgEquiv.ofRingEquiv upgrades it to an A-algebra equivalence. No data are chosen from an unproved existence theorem inside a definition: all existential witnesses are eliminated inside this theorem proof.

source.place: Tag 030C; elementary transport of the given algebra structure
